tools.name: search_analytics
tools.description: Query Google Search Console search analytics and return ranked clicks, impressions, CTR, and position

siteUrl.description: Search Console property, such as https://example.com/ or sc-domain:example.com

startDate.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to 28 days ago

endDate.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to today

startRow.description: Zero-based row to start from, for paging through a large result

maxTableRows.description: Cap rows shown in the text table; structured rows are always complete. 0 = summary only.

type.description: Result type. discover is the Discover feed and googleNews is the Google News app and news.google.com, not the News tab in Search. Both support fewer dimensions than web: neither reports a query dimension

dataState.description: full = finalized data (default, ~2-3 day lag); all = include recent partial data

tools.name: keyword_ideas
tools.description: Expand a seed with free Google Autocomplete suggestions and optionally cross-reference Search Console rankings; no extra API key needed

siteUrl.description: Optional Search Console property used to identify queries already ranking

language.description: Autocomplete interface language passed as hl

expansions.description: Suggestion expansion families to run beyond the bare seed

days.description: Search Console lookback window in days

tools.name: search_opportunities
tools.description: Find queries ranking just off page 1 with high impressions, the highest-ROI keywords to improve

startDate.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to the latest 28-day window

endDate.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to today

minPosition.description: Lowest average position to include; defaults to 5

maxPosition.description: Highest average position to include; defaults to 20

limit.description: Maximum opportunities to return; defaults to 50

tools.name: compare_search_periods
tools.description: Compare an analysis window with the preceding equal period to identify search gainers and losers

startDate.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to the latest 28-day window

endDate.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to today

limit.description: Maximum gainers and losers to return; defaults to 50 each

tools.name: ctr_gaps
tools.description: Find high-impression queries or pages whose CTR trails peers at the same position for snippet rewrite prioritization

startDate.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to the latest 28-day window

endDate.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to today

by.description: Dimension used to identify CTR gaps

limit.description: Maximum gaps to return; defaults to 50

tools.name: query_cannibalization
tools.description: Find queries served by multiple pages to prioritize consolidation and internal-linking decisions

startDate.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to the latest 28-day window

endDate.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to today

minImpressions.description: Minimum impressions per query-page row; defaults to 10

tools.name: list_sitemaps
tools.description: List sitemaps submitted for a Google Search Console property

tools.name: list_properties
tools.description: List Google Search Console properties the service account can access, with permission levels

tools.name: submit_sitemap
tools.description: Submit a sitemap to Google Search Console and return its current state

feedpath.description: Absolute URL of the sitemap to submit

dryRun.description: If true, report what would be submitted without writing to Search Console

tools.name: delete_sitemap
tools.description: Remove a submitted sitemap from a Search Console property (write; supports dryRun)

feedpath.description: Absolute URL of the sitemap to remove

dryRun.description: If true, report what would be removed without writing to Search Console

tools.name: inspect_url
tools.description: Inspect a URL's Google index status, canonical selection, mobile usability, and rich results

siteUrl.description: Search Console property containing the inspected URL

tools.name: index_coverage
tools.description: Check how many of a sitemap's pages are indexed by Google (bounded; respects URL Inspection quota)

siteUrl.description: Search Console property containing the sitemap URLs

sitemapUrl.description: Fully qualified sitemap URL to inspect

tools.name: request_recrawl
tools.description: Inspect URLs' Google index status and resubmit the covering sitemap for the ones not indexed, the supported bulk recrawl nudge (write; supports dryRun)

siteUrl.description: Search Console property containing the URLs

urls.description: Explicit URLs to check; omit to read them from sitemapUrl

sitemapUrl.description: Sitemap to read URLs from; also the default sitemap to resubmit

feedpath.description: Sitemap to resubmit when unindexed URLs are found; defaults to sitemapUrl

dryRun.description: If true, inspect and report without resubmitting the sitemap

tools.name: indexnow_submit
tools.description: Submit changed URLs in bulk to IndexNow search engines: Bing, Yandex, Naver, Seznam, Yep; not Google. Needs an IndexNow key hosted on the site at https://<host>/<key>.txt (write; supports dryRun)

urls.description: Changed page URLs; one submission covers one host

key.description: IndexNow key; defaults to SEO_MCP_INDEXNOW_KEY. The same key must be hosted on the site as a text file at https://<host>/<key>.txt (or at keyLocation) containing only the key

keyLocation.description: URL of the hosted key file when it is not https://<host>/<key>.txt

endpoint.description: IndexNow endpoint to notify; participating engines share submissions

dryRun.description: If true, report what would be submitted without notifying the endpoint

tools.name: pagespeed
tools.description: Run PageSpeed Insights for field Core Web Vitals, Lighthouse scores, and top opportunities

apiKey.description: Optional PageSpeed Insights API key; defaults to SEO_MCP_PAGESPEED_KEY

tools.name: seo_audit
tools.description: Fetch and audit a web page's on-page SEO without Google credentials

tools.name: audit_site
tools.description: Audit the on-page SEO of up to N pages from a sitemap and roll up the most common issues across the site. Takes a sitemap URL rather than a Search Console property, and needs no Google credentials

tools.name: server_version
tools.description: Report which build of this server is answering, where it is running from, and whether it came out of an npx cache. Four values look like this one and are not: what npm calls latest, what the version range resolves to, what the plugin manifest declares, and what is actually running. Checking the command-line tool is not a substitute, since it is a separate process resolved separately. No credentials needed; read-only

tools.name: wporg_plugin
tools.description: Look up a WordPress.org plugin's install base, downloads, ratings, and support stats by slug; public API, no credentials or API key needed

downloadDays.description: Days of daily download history to fetch; 0 skips it

includeVersionDistribution.description: Also fetch the share of active installs on each plugin version

tools.name: play_store_stats
tools.description: Read Google Play bulk reports for an app: active device installs and store-listing visitors and acquisitions by traffic source. installsDimension picks which installs breakdown is read (overview, country, language, device, os_version, carrier or app_version), include adds the ratings, crashes and reviews report families, and startDate with endDate reads every month the window touches instead of the single month in month. Reads the reporting bucket named by SEO_MCP_PLAY_BUCKET; read-only

month.description: Report month as YYYYMM; defaults to the current UTC month. Ignored when startDate and endDate are given

installsDimension.description: Which installs report to read. overview is undocumented by Google but present in real buckets; the others are the documented breakdowns

include.description: Extra report families to read. Missing files are normal: Google emits a report only when there is something to report

storePerformanceDimension.description: Which store performance breakdown to read

storePerformanceTotals.description: Read the total_ variant instead. It is a different report, not a rollup of the same one: it carries acquisitions only, with no visitors and no conversion rate, and for some apps it covers far fewer dates and attributes every acquisition to a placeholder source

startDate.description: Window start in YYYY-MM-DD. With endDate, reads every month the window touches and filters rows to it

tools.name: app_store_listing
tools.description: Read an App Store listing's indexed fields per locale (name, subtitle, keywords) against Apple's character limits, plus promotional text, version state and star ratings. The ratings come from the public storefront lookup because App Store Connect exposes no aggregate rating; each entry names its source. Needs SEO_MCP_ASC_KEY_PATH, SEO_MCP_ASC_KEY_ID and SEO_MCP_ASC_ISSUER_ID; read-only

appId.description: App Store Connect numeric app id; provide this or bundleId

bundleId.description: Bundle id, resolved to an app id when appId is not given; provide this or appId

platform.description: App Store platform whose version is read

state.description: Read the live listing or the editable one being prepared for release

storefronts.description: Storefront country codes for the public ratings lookup

tools.name: app_store_sales
tools.description: Read App Store Sales and Trends: units downloaded per day per territory per app, summarized by SKU. Needs SEO_MCP_ASC_VENDOR_NUMBER and a team key with Admin, Finance or Sales and Reports. A period with no sales is reported as an absence rather than an error. Read-only

reportDate.description: Report date. DAILY and WEEKLY take YYYY-MM-DD (WEEKLY means the week's ending date), MONTHLY takes YYYY-MM, YEARLY takes YYYY. Defaults to the most recent complete period for the frequency

version.description: Report version, such as 1_0 or 1_3, when the default is not accepted

includeRows.description: Include every raw report row as well as the per-SKU summary

tools.name: play_vitals
tools.description: Read Android vitals from the Play Developer Reporting API: crash rate, ANR rate, error counts and startup metrics, daily or hourly, with optional breakdowns. Reports how fresh the data actually is. Carries no acquisition or conversion data; use play_store_stats for that. Read-only

metricSets.description: Which Android vitals metric sets to query

aggregationPeriod.description: DAILY is reported in America/Los_Angeles, HOURLY in UTC

days.description: How many days back to query

dimensions.description: Breakdown dimensions such as versionCode or countryCode

includeRows.description: Include every raw row as well as the counts; off by default so a summary call stays small

tools.name: app_store_discovery
tools.description: Read the App Store surfaces beyond the listing text: search keywords, app tags, product page optimization experiments, custom product pages, in-app events, territory availability and review summarizations. A resource this key cannot read is reported as unavailable rather than as empty. Read-only

appId.description: App Store Connect numeric app id; provide this or bundleId

bundleId.description: Bundle id; provide this or appId

include.description: Which discovery surfaces to read; empty reads all of them

locales.description: Locales for per-locale resources such as searchKeywords

platform.description: Platform for resources that require one

includeRows.description: Include every raw row as well as the counts; off by default so a summary call stays small

tools.name: app_store_reviews
tools.description: Read App Store customer reviews and your responses, filtered by rating or storefront. Reports the mean and star split of the reviews actually fetched, which is not the app's lifetime rating; App Store Connect exposes no aggregate rating resource. Read-only

appId.description: App Store Connect numeric app id; provide this or bundleId

bundleId.description: Bundle id; provide this or appId

sort.description: Sort order; newest first by default

limit.description: Maximum reviews to return across pages

tools.name: crux_field_data
tools.description: Read real-user Core Web Vitals for an origin or URL from the Chrome UX Report: the current 28-day field record with p75s and histograms. Field data, not a lab test; PageSpeed's own field block is being discontinued. Needs SEO_MCP_CRUX_KEY or a PageSpeed key allowed to call the Chrome UX Report API; read-only

origin.description: Origin such as https://example.com; aggregates every page under it. Give origin or url, not both

url.description: A single page URL. Give origin or url, not both

formFactor.description: Device class; omit for all form factors combined

metrics.description: Metric names to request; omit for all available

tools.name: crux_history
tools.description: Read the Chrome UX Report weekly history for an origin or URL, roughly six months of 28-day rolling windows, so a field metric can be seen trending rather than as one point. Read-only

origin.description: Origin such as https://example.com; aggregates every page under it. Give origin or url, not both

url.description: A single page URL. Give origin or url, not both

formFactor.description: Device class; omit for all form factors combined

metrics.description: Metric names to request; omit for all available

collectionPeriodCount.description: Weekly periods to return, 1 to 40. Documented history is about six months; the API decides what it actually has

tools.name: ads_campaigns
tools.description: Read Google Ads campaigns: status, daily budget, impressions, clicks, cost and conversions over a window. Needs GOOGLE_ADS_DEVELOPER_TOKEN, an OAuth client and a refresh token; read-only

days.description: How many days back to report, ending today

tools.name: ads_keywords
tools.description: Read every Google Ads keyword with its effective CPC bid, approval and serving status, and metrics. Returns every row rather than a first page, which is how a count taken from the console goes wrong; read-only

days.description: How many days back to report, ending today

status.description: Limit to one keyword state. Omitted, every keyword is returned with its state named, because dropping rows silently is how a count taken from this tool goes wrong the way a console count does

tools.name: ads_ads
tools.description: Read Google Ads ads with ad strength, policy approval status, serving status and metrics; read-only

days.description: How many days back to report, ending today

tools.name: ads_ad_copy
tools.description: Read what a Google Ads ad actually says: every headline and description with its pinning and Google's performance label, the display path, the final URLs, and the policy topics behind a limited or disapproved status rather than only the status word. Also reports headline text shared by more than one ad, since two ads in an ad group with the same headlines are not testing anything against each other. Assets such as sitelinks and promotions are not read here; read-only

adGroup.description: Limit to one ad group by name. Omitted, every ad in the account is read, which is what answers whether a headline is repeated across ad groups

adId.description: Limit to one ad by its numeric id, for reading back the copy that was supposed to ship

includeRemoved.description: Include removed ads. Off by default: a removed ad's copy is history, and it crowds out the ads that are serving

tools.name: ads_assets
tools.description: Read the sitelinks, callouts, structured snippets, promotions, prices, call and image assets attached to the account, its campaigns and its ad groups, with what each one actually says rather than only its type and id. An account-level asset applies to every campaign, so it is listed even when one campaign is named: an ad that looks bare in ads_ad_copy may be serving with these beside it. Attached is not shown, and a level that cannot be read is reported as an error in place rather than as nothing attached; read-only

campaign.description: Limit campaign and ad group assets to one campaign by name. Account-level assets are still listed, because they apply to every campaign including this one

type.description: Limit to one asset type. Omitted, every type is listed, including types this tool has no shaped reading for

includeRemoved.description: Include links whose status is removed. Off by default: a removed asset is history and crowds out the ones that can serve

tools.name: ads_query
tools.description: Run an arbitrary GAQL SELECT against the Google Ads account for a question the shaped reads do not cover. GAQL has no statement other than SELECT, so this cannot change anything; read-only

query.description: A GAQL SELECT statement. GAQL has no other statement, so this cannot change anything

tools.name: ads_search_terms
tools.description: Read the queries that actually triggered an ad, with the keyword each one matched and its metrics. This is the paid equivalent of the Search Console query dimension. Google withholds terms too few people searched, so an absent term is unknown rather than absent; read-only

days.description: How many days back to report, ending today

minCost.description: Drop search terms that cost less than this over the window

minImpressions.description: Drop search terms below this many impressions

zeroConversionsOnly.description: Keep only terms that converted nothing, which is the list that feeds negative keywords

tools.name: ads_negatives
tools.description: Read the negative keywords already in place, at campaign, ad group or shared-set level. A negative blocks traffic without leaving any record that it did, so this is what to check when a keyword stops serving and nothing looks wrong, and what to check before adding a term twice; read-only

level.description: Which negatives to read. A term blocked at campaign level is blocked everywhere in it; a shared set applies to every campaign it is attached to

tools.name: ads_changes
tools.description: Read the Google Ads change history: what changed, when, which fields, by whom, and whether it came from a tool or from someone in the browser. Google keeps 30 days and at most 10,000 rows, so an empty result over a longer window is a limit rather than a finding. Filter on resourceType rather than on changed field names: a budget change reports amountMicros and says neither budget nor status. This is the audit trail for anything ads_update writes; read-only

days.description: How many days of change history to read, ending now. Google keeps 30 days and refuses more

tools.name: ads_negatives_update
tools.description: Add or remove negative keywords in a batch, enumerated one by one with no pattern form. Before adding, every proposed negative is checked against the campaign's own live keywords and the batch is refused if one would block traffic, because a wrong negative leaves no evidence anywhere: the traffic just stops. Dry run unless dryRun is false, and the terms are read back afterwards

action.description: Add negative keywords or remove existing ones. Removal matters as much as adding: a wrong negative shows up as nothing at all

level.description: Where the negatives live. A campaign-level negative blocks the term everywhere in that campaign

target.description: The campaign or ad group name. It must match exactly one or nothing is changed

keywords.description: The negative terms, enumerated one by one. There is no pattern or match-all form: a selector is one typo away from blocking a whole campaign

matchType.description: How each term blocks. BROAD blocks any query containing all its words, which is the setting that can silently kill a campaign

dryRun.description: Report what would change, and which proposed negatives would block a live keyword, without changing anything

confirm.description: Perform the batch even though a guard tripped. The dry run lists what tripped, so this confirms something already read

tools.name: ads_update
tools.description: Change one Google Ads keyword bid, campaign daily budget, campaign status, ad status or keyword status. Pausing one keyword is its own kind because dropping a bid is not the same thing: the keyword stays eligible and goes on competing for the same budget. Spends money, so it is a dry run unless dryRun is false, it refuses a change that trips a guard unless confirm is true, and it re-reads the value after writing because an accepted request is not a stored value. Guards: more than three times the current amount, more than $25, or pausing something that is serving

kind.description: What to change: a keyword's max CPC bid, a campaign's daily budget, a campaign's status, an ad's status, or a keyword's status. Use keywordStatus to stop one keyword serving; dropping its bid is not the same thing, because the keyword stays eligible and keeps competing for the same budget

target.description: The keyword text, the campaign name, or the numeric ad id. It must match exactly one thing or the call is refused

value.description: The new amount in dollars for a bid or budget, or pause or enable for a status

dryRun.description: Report what would change and which guards it trips, without changing anything. On by default: this tool spends money, so performing a change has to be asked for

confirm.description: Perform a change that trips a guard. Ignored on a dry run. The dry run lists the guard reasons, so this confirms something already read rather than something unseen

tools.name: ads_keyword_create
tools.description: Add one keyword to an ad group. This is the only tool here that creates rather than changes, and it is guarded differently for that reason: there is no current value to compare against, so it is a duplicate check instead. It refuses a keyword that already exists in the target ad group, including a removed one, since a removed criterion still holds the text and Google rejects the create with an error naming a resource the interface does not show. A copy elsewhere in the account trips a guard rather than refusing, because two copies compete for the same budget. EXACT by default; PHRASE and BROAD buy more than the text written and each trips a guard. Dry run unless dryRun is false, and the keyword is read back afterwards

keyword.description: The keyword text to add. It is created as written; this tool does not guess at variants

adGroup.description: The ad group to add it to. It must match exactly one or nothing is added

bid.description: The max CPC bid in dollars. There is no current bid to compare against on a create, so the only size check is the ceiling

matchType.description: How the keyword matches. EXACT by default because it is the one that buys what it says; PHRASE and BROAD buy more than the text written here and each trips a guard

dryRun.description: Report what would be added and which guards it trips, without adding anything

confirm.description: Add it even though a guard tripped. The dry run lists every reason, so this confirms something already read

tools.name: ads_update_batch
tools.description: Change several Google Ads keyword bids, or several campaign daily budgets, in one call. It is a named list of pairs, not a rule applied to many things: each entry names one target and the value it should end at, and an entry that matches no row or more than one refuses the whole batch before anything is written. The sum is guarded as well as each entry, because separately reasonable raises are one large spend change together. Dry run unless dryRun is false, and every value is read back afterwards

kind.description: One kind per call. A summed guard is only honest inside one kind: bids and budgets sum to dollars, statuses do not, and mixing them makes the total unreadable

changes.description: A named list of pairs, each with its own value. There is no selector form: enumeration cannot make the mistake that a pattern can

dryRun.description: Resolve and price every entry and report the total, without changing anything

confirm.description: Perform the batch even though a guard tripped. The dry run lists every reason, so this confirms something already read

tools.name: list_snapshots
tools.description: List the snapshot documents already in the snapshot directory, newest first: when each was taken, the window it covers, and how many properties, apps, packages and plugins it holds. This is what says whether there is an earlier snapshot to compare against and what to name as from and to; a file that does not parse is listed with its error rather than hidden; read-only

limit.description: Maximum snapshots to return, newest first

tools.name: snapshot
tools.description: Capture four surfaces in one timestamped document: Search Console totals and top rows per property, App Store listings, Google Play installs and traffic, and WordPress.org stats. Core Web Vitals field data, Android vitals, App Store sales and App Store reviews are not captured. A surface that cannot be read is recorded as an error in place rather than omitted; list_snapshots names the documents already on disk to compare an earlier one against; read-only

apps.description: App Store apps, each a numeric app id or a bundle id

windowDays.description: Search Console window in days, ending today

platform.description: App Store platform for the app surfaces

storefronts.description: Storefront country codes for App Store ratings

outPath.description: File name or path inside the snapshot directory (SEO_MCP_SNAPSHOT_DIR, default ~/.config/seo-mcp/snapshots); must end in .json, or pass auto to name the file after the moment it was taken. An existing file is not overwritten unless overwrite is true

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at outPath; without it an existing file is left alone and reported

tools.name: compare_snapshots
tools.description: Compare two snapshot documents and return the differences between them: clicks, impressions, positions, installs, ratings and locale counts. Reports arithmetic only, never whether a change was good or what caused it; read-only

from.description: Snapshot file name or path inside the snapshot directory; latest names the newest snapshot on disk and previous the one before it

to.description: Snapshot file name or path inside the snapshot directory; latest names the newest snapshot on disk and previous the one before it

minImpressions.description: Ignore page position moves below this many impressions on both sides
